summary: OAuth for Stripe Apps lets users install your app and grant it access to their account. You build the app with the Stripe CLI, set stripe_api_access_type to oauth and distribution_type to public in the manifest, test it with external test links, then submit it for review to publish on the Stripe App Marketplace. Authorization codes last 5 minutes, access tokens 1 hour and refresh tokens 1 year.
key_facts: This guide covers Stripe Apps OAuth (install links) — not the older Connect OAuth flow
Manifest must set stripe_api_access_type=oauth, distribution_type=public and allowed_redirect_uris (the first is the default redirect)
You can test before publishing via the External test tab (test OAuth links; different links exist for live, test and sandbox)
Public OAuth install links do not work until the app is published; Stripe's review team can still install and test via that link
Authorization codes are one-time use and valid for 5 minutes; the backend exchanges them using your secret API key
Access tokens expire in 1 hour; refresh tokens expire after 1 year and are rolled on every exchange
Live-mode redirect_uri must use HTTPS; redirect_uri must exactly match one in the manifest

steps.title: Create the Stripe App
steps.description: Install the Stripe CLI and run `stripe apps create <app-name>`.

steps.title: Configure the manifest for OAuth
steps.description: Set stripe_api_access_type to oauth, distribution_type to public and allowed_redirect_uris (for Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback); add the permissions your app needs.

steps.title: Upload and run an external test
steps.description: Run `stripe apps upload`, open the app details page, and use the External test tab to get test OAuth links.

steps.title: Build the install link and exchange codes
steps.description: Redirect users to https://marketplace.stripe.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=…&redirect_uri=…&state=… then POST the one-time code (5 min) to https://api.stripe.com/v1/oauth/token using your secret key.
warnings: Use the API key that matches the link type (live, test or sandbox)

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.description: Submit the app for Marketplace review, providing an install URL that starts the onboarding/installation flow using the public OAuth links from the Settings tab.

blockers.title: Public links are inactive until publish
blockers.description: The public OAuth install links do not work until the app is published, so you must use external test links while developing.
blockers.workaround: Use the External test tab links; Stripe reviewers can install via the public link during review.

blockers.title: Review timeline unknown
blockers.description: Stripe publishes no review duration on the pages checked.
